result.summary:
D-085 DD1 is implemented in the M7 prototype, and the design is written up as section 12 of docs/m7-plan/morale-proposal.md. It is marked PROPOSAL wherever it is design; statements it overrides are struck or narrowed in place with dated bold notes (list in section 12.9).

(a) Fighting report (DD1-R2 (a)): both resolvers now give BattleResult.FirstFightMs (null means no fighting). It is set at the code points that already count an attack:
- TacticalResolver: a melee blow; a fired missile shot, hit or miss; a crew-served or domain weapon shot at an enemy entity, hull or airframe; a boarding fight; a ram, breach or glance.
- AutoResolver: melee in contact and volleys.
Two edge cases are labelled READINGs:
- MOR3-R1 (a): a bombard of a bare point counts as fighting only if its blast reaches an enemy entity or hull.
- MOR3-R2 (a): a bow contact that is not a ram is not fighting.
Measured first-fight instants per domain: melee 148,000 ms; missile 0; guns 0; aircraft 14,000; boarding 26,000; ram 198,000. On lane P's tuning battery (1,600 cases per resolver) the report never disagrees with the attack count.

(b) Settlement (DD1-R1 (a), read per battle): a battle with fighting settles as before. A battle without fighting changes no army's morale: no entry cost, no DR29 decrease, no DA1 rise, though the reported winner is still recorded. The settlement row gains Fought (codec version 3, 111 bytes). Measured: MOR2's unfought mutual rout and unfought withdrawal now leave both armies unchanged (they were +150,000 and −50,000), and so does an unfought decisive win. Boundary: one missed arrow means both armies drop 800,000 → 750,000; no attack means no change. A formation that entered a fought battle without striking pays the entry cost (910,000 with the rise).

(c) In-battle part, PROPOSAL C1, default 0: the charge falls at the battle's first fighting instant, before that instant's routs; a later arrival pays at its own entry; nobody pays in a battle without fighting. Measured turn-exact in both resolvers: identical to the part-off battle before the first fight. An unfought battle produces the same result hash and trace hash as with the part off.

(d) War Sandbox: DD1 reaches it through the resolvers (measured). Lane S siege battles: PROPOSAL (a), not implemented.

Tests: NoFightingTests (21 methods, 30 cases). Battery: the default digests are unchanged; with the part on, the digests and outcome counts are re-measured. Rule P1 is 16/20 off, 14/20 on and 13/20 with c = 200. Lane P acceptance stays OPEN.

Mutants: 36 run, 35 killed by named semantic tests. R3 survived and is argued equivalent, backed by an instrumentation run (0 line misses in the full suite or in 3,200 battery battles).
not_done: Lane S siege battles: DD1 is a PROPOSAL only (proposal §12.6). The stand-in resolves no attack and never reaches the campaign settlement.
War Sandbox: the result inspection showing the first fighting instant and the DD1-aware settlement preview are a PROPOSAL, not implemented.
Switching on the in-battle part of the entry cost (default stays 0) with a battery re-measurement and AutoResolver re-fit is deferred to M7.14 / D-079 Q4.
Lane MOR2's measurement of the rout-versus-withdrawal parity gap in persons with the part on was not repeated under C1 (it was measured with the charge at entry).
Lane P held-out acceptance battery: not run.
Aggregation of settlement over several formations per army (M7.15): not built. Under DD1-R1 (a) it needs only one fought input per battle.
Equivalent mutants E1 and E2: not run (argued equivalent). The state-hash appends for the first fight and charge instants were not mutated.
Independent verification of this lane: not run.
open_questions: READING MOR3-R3 (applied (a)): DD1 is applied to morale only. Lane W's collapse still deserts routed men in a battle without fighting: 800 of 2,000 per side in the measured unfought mutual rout from 500. The in-battle recovery also still runs before the first fight. Alternative (b): freeze in-battle morale until the first fight. Presented as an observation; no Director question is invented.
READING MOR3-R1 (bare-point bombard): (a) applied, fighting only when the blast reaches an enemy entity or hull. Alternative (b): every round counts.
READING MOR3-R2 (bow contact that is not a ram): (a) applied, no fighting. Alternative (b): it counts as an attack.

Why more battery outcomes change under C1 than with the charge at entry is INFERRED, not measured: a charge taken at entry could be recovered while a formation held before the fight; one taken at the first fight cannot.
proposals_for_director: PROPOSAL C1 for the in-battle part of the entry cost (D-085 §4's first form): charge at the battle's first fighting instant, at its own entry for a later arrival after it, never in a battle without fighting. Alternative C2: drop the in-battle part. C3 (charge at entry, refund if unfought) fails D-085 §4.

Siege PROPOSAL (a): when the land module resolves siege battles (C15, ADR-060 §2.5), DD1 applies through the same fought report. That covers the campaign settlement and lane S's three siege-morale event terms (repelled-assault lift and shock, failed-relief shock). Alternative (b), not proposed: a fought test inside the stand-in now.
Sandbox PROPOSAL: the inspection shows the first fighting instant or 'no fighting: no morale change'. The Campaign Encounter settlement preview applies DD1 with the same functions.
No new Director question: every design item here is delegated by D-085 §4. The observations are in proposal §12.8 and report §10.

I verified lane MOR3 at f84b941 in a fresh worktree I cloned myself, /home/user/m7w/verify-MOR3-r1. No earlier verifier directory existed. HEAD stayed at f84b941 throughout, and git status was clean at the end.

Verdict: every brief item is implemented as claimed, and the production code matches D-085 on reading. I found no blocker and no major. Three findings are minor and five are nits.

**What the code does (checked by reading it)**
- **Fought report.** FirstFightMs is set at every attack-count site in both resolvers. All attack events are in EventClass.Fire (30), which runs before Resolve (50), and a landing (Arrival, 10) also runs before Resolve.
- **Settlement.** The three terms are gated with IfFought. BattleFighting reads the battle, not the formation. The Fought byte is in codec v3, 111 bytes per row.
- **In-battle part (C1).** It is charged at the start of Resolve in the tactical resolver and at the start of phase 5 in the AutoResolver. Before the first fight it only records the entry.
- **War Sandbox.** It settles nothing.
- **Siege.** The stand-in is FormationAssaultStandIn, with siege-morale constants of 50, 100 and 400 per mille, as the report cites.
- **E1 and E2.** The lane argued two mutants equivalent without running them (E1: a friendly land entity never sits in a bare-point blast, because of DangerClose; E2: in the AutoResolver the in-contact volley's fought call always follows the melee's). | Finding | Severity | Verdict | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| R1-01 | minor | REPRODUCED | Fixed in tests. V1, V2 and this round's V1b (the second early return) survived the full suite (1553/1553). On the walled battle: 540 Fire events, all blocked; 0 attacks; FirstFightMs null; settles Fought 0 at 800,000; yet the trace oracle listed all 540. V2 was shown non-equivalent on a battle behind buildings: FirstFightMs 0 and 3 charges. The trace oracle is now validated against the battle's attack count, and a line-of-fire oracle recomputes each shot from outside the rule. New tests: wall and buildings (TacticalResolver); buildings (AutoResolver, both resolvers agreeing). V1, V1b and V2 are now killed. |
| R1-02 | minor | REPRODUCED | Fixed with three new pins. V5a, V5c and V6 survived. Non-equivalence was measured for all three, including V5c, which the verifier could not show: a field gun's case moves from 0 to 16,000-104,000. Pins: a helicopter rocket at a land entity that misses (FirstFightMs 0); a field-gun round landing 23,343 mm from a lone rifleman, beyond its 15,000 mm blast (FirstFightMs 0); a boarding fight with no casualties (26,000). V5a, V5c and V6 are now killed. |

Walled setup, seeds 1-3: the TacticalResolver ends in a Standoff with no fighting; the AutoResolver's FirstFightMs is 0, it ends SideEliminated, and the default policy picks Auto. Cause (CITED): the AutoResolver's contact and line of fire ignore walls. Recorded as a limitation and a lane P parity item (PROPOSAL). Added a cross-resolver test where the two agree (buildings). | R1-07 | nit | REPRODUCED | Relabelled DERIVED in report section 5 and proposal section 12.4. The bench runs no settlement. |
